Create a 15-second horizontal 16:9 live-action cinematic sequence.

Zahhak’s coverage is slow, composed and slightly low-angle.

Use hard cuts only at the specified shot boundaries.

Jamshid is already lying restrained on the machine’s broad stationary work surface.

His body remains in exactly the same position throughout this block.

The work surface does not translate, slide or feed forward.
It is not a conveyor belt.
Jamshid does not travel past the blade.
He does not pass beside it.
There is no transport journey toward the machine.

Preserve the established alignment of the body, work surface and cutting mechanism from the reference and preceding setup. Do not introduce a new machine layout.

Only the cutting mechanism operates.
The table and Jamshid remain stationary.
No blade-to-body contact is shown.

Night inside one vast collection hall.

The industrial timber saw stands in the central floor area.
Collection objects occupy display furniture along the perimeter walls.
The balcony opening is at the NORTH end of the hall.

Cold integrated ceiling lights illuminate the interior.
Small neutral display lights skim the objects.
One harder neutral task lamp illuminates Jamshid and the machine.
All light sources remain steady.

The balcony has weak cool exterior illumination and fixed rail lights.

In the frontal shot of Zahhak, the camera faces back into the hall. Only the interior appears behind him; the exterior is behind the camera.

START STATE AND BLOCKING
Jamshid lies on his back on the stationary machine work surface.

His existing restraints remain secured.
His RIGHT arm is free to perform the final command.
His left arm stays beside his body.

Guard A stands beside the work surface.
Guard B remains at the controls.
Neither guard moves the table or transports Jamshid.

Jamshid has turned his head slightly toward the NORTH balcony route, where Zahhak has gone.

Zahhak is approaching the balcony rail.

75mm tight oblique close-up beside the blade housing.

Keep Jamshid outside this tight frame.

No sliding platform.
No contact.

Hard cut to Jamshid.

65mm intimate handheld close-up from the NORTH side of the work surface, slightly above Jamshid’s face, looking diagonally down toward him.

Frame his masked face, visible eyes, upper chest and enough space in the lower foreground for his RIGHT hand to enter.

His head rests against the surface.
His body remains fully stationary.

His face is turned toward the camera.
His eyes are fixed just beyond the lens, toward the place where Zahhak disappeared.

His breathing is shallow.

His gaze stays forward toward the exterior beyond the camera.

He never turns toward Jamshid.

24mm from BEHIND Zahhak at the balcony doorway.

His back faces the camera.
His staff is planted.
His weight is settled.

A slow crane rise reveals the active harbor and city below beyond his shoulders.

Keep the movement measured and continuous.

Zahhak remains still, looking down at ordinary life.

His snakes continue small living movements.

The machine remains inside the hall, behind the camera and entirely out of view.

END STATE AND EDIT
The final image of Jamshid was his unanswered raised RIGHT hand in sharp focus, with his fixed gaze softly visible behind it.

Jamshid and the machine work surface never changed position.

Zahhak stands at the balcony rail, facing the city.
He has not looked back or acknowledged Jamshid.

The machine continues audibly off-screen.

Continuous mechanical motor and cutting mechanism.
No second switch activation.

During Jamshid’s close-up:
shallow breathing;
slight clothing tension as his right arm rises;
quiet restraint friction;
the uninterrupted machine nearby.

During Zahhak’s shots:
measured staff contact;
uneven footsteps;
restrained costume movement;
harbor activity becoming clearer outside.

No bodily impacts.
No anatomical sounds.
No scream.
No dramatic sound accent on the raised hand.
